title: Windowed Percentile PI (WPPI) Autoscaler for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: current autoscalers either react too slowly to short bursts or aggressively oscillate on noisy tail-latency signals. For Dedicated customers we must simultaneously preserve latency SLOs (p95/p99), provide contractual throughput guarantees, and keep unit costs predictable.

Proposal: design and implement a Windowed Percentile Proportional-Integral (WPPI) autoscaler tailored for dedicated GPU fleets. WPPI uses windowed percentile estimators of observed latency and effective throughput (token/sec and request/sec) to derive a headroom signal, applies a PI controller on that percentile headroom, and combines it with a budgeted-burst mechanism and safety fences (slew-rate, minimum hold, rollback contracts). Key features:
- Target metrics: windowed p95 latency, windowed median concurrency, observed effective throughput (tokens/sec), and kv-cache affinity score per instance pool.
- Algorithm: compute percentile headroom = target_latency / observed_percentile_latency, feed proportional + integral terms that operate on percentile headroom rather than raw latency to reduce sensitivity to outliers. Apply a smoothing window (configurable 30s–5m) and percentile selector (p90/p95/p99 per shape).
- Burst budget: track a per-tenant and per-fleet burst credit pool funded by steady-state overprovision. Allow short-duration scale-ups beyond steady targets bounded by credits and global surge caps.
- Safety limits: max 50% scale-up in a single step (configurable), slew-rate gating, cooldown windows, minimum instance hold for scale-down (configurable by SKU), and an emergency rollback contract that pins capacity to last-good if SLO degradation is detected during rollout.
- KV affinity-aware scale-down: prefer evicting instances with low KV-affinity score to reduce cold-KV warming, and introduce a 'swap' heuristic that rebalances requests before eviction to minimize KV re-population costs.
- Operational surfaces: configurable controller parameters per-tenant/plan, telemetry dashboards for controller signals (headroom, p-term, i-term, burst credits), canary rollout and automatic rollback hooks, and integration with Console release/rollout flows.

Why different: WPPI operates on percentile-derived headroom and integrates a bounded budget model for bursts plus explicit KV-affinity-aware slow-down to avoid cache churn — combining control-theory stability with workload economics and runtime data-awareness.
acceptance_criteria: WPPI controller implemented in autoscaler service with feature flag behind 'wppi_v1'
Controller exposes config knobs (window length, percentile, P/I gains, max-step, min-hold) via fleet config API
Load-test harness (k8s e2e) demonstrates p95 SLO maintained within target +/-10% during synthetic burst scenarios while reducing cold-KV repopulation events by >=25% compared to baseline autoscaler
Burst budget mechanism respects per-tenant and global caps and reports credit usage metrics to metrics pipeline
Safe rollout plan: canary on 5% of a dedicated fleet; automatic rollback if error rate or SLO breach exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive windows
Console shows new controller metrics and a toggle for 'WPPI' with per-fleet overrides
Operator runbook updated with troubleshooting steps and escalation (links included)
technical_notes: Percentile headroom = (SLO_latency_ms) / (observed_percentile_latency_ms + epsilon). Running the PI loop on headroom reduces amplifying outlier noise.
Choose integral windup guard: decay integral state after sustained positive headroom to prevent excessive accumulated credit when load drops abruptly.
Burst credits: represent time-weighted excess tokens serviced; credits decay with policy and require accounting at per-tenant granularity for multi-tenant fleets.
KV-affinity: affinity score derived from recent cache hit rate + hitchance metric. Score in [0,1] used to rank instance eviction preference.
Slew-rate gating: enforce both absolute instance delta cap and percent cap within control window. Default: max(3 instances, 50% of current) per scale step.
Configuration precedence: fleet-level override > tenant plan default > global default. Defaults should be conservative to prioritize stability.
Expose controller internal metrics: headroom, p_term, i_term, requested_capacity, applied_capacity, burst_credit_balance, kv_affinity_histogram. Tag by fleet_id and tenant_id.
implementation_plan: Week 1: design doc + review with runtime and SRE (align on metrics/shape).
Week 2: prototype controller logic in autoscaler service (no-op scale decisions logged).
Week 3: integrate burst-credit accounting and KV-affinity ranking; unit tests for edge cases (integral windup, burst exhaustion).
Week 4: e2e load tests in staging using synthetic workloads (spiky, sawtooth, long-tail); tune default gains.
Week 5: Console integration and dashboard panels; operator runbook draft; security review (if needed).
Week 6: Canary rollout (5% of capacity) with monitoring playbook; iterate on tuning; full fleet rollout after 2 canary cycles without regressions.
test_plan: Unit tests for PI loop with varying noise profiles and sudden step inputs
Integration tests verifying burst-credit accounting across simulated tenants
Staging scenarios: 1) 30s micro-burst (10x) 2) Slow ramp (10 min) 3) KV-churn scenario (cache invalidation) 4) Multi-tenant noisy tails
Quantified checks: p95 within target +/-10%, scale oscillation count reduced vs baseline, cost delta tracked across test windows
Chaos: simulate instance loss during scale-up and ensure graceful rollback and credit reconciliation
